title: Service-member record access can expose both privacy failure and processing delay while correction and claimant outcomes remain open
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-107784 review of Department of Defense release of service-member personnel and health records
geography: United States Department of Defense and military-service personnel and health-record release systems

observations.period: Fiscal years 2021–2025 breach review, GAO covert test, and October 16, 2026 report

denominator.unit: personnel-record requests in GAO's covert test of DOD internal controls

reported_improper_releases.unit: almost 50 improper releases reported by military services during fiscal years 2021–2025, affecting more than 1,000 service members

covert_test_processing.unit: requests processed out of 26 in GAO's covert test

covert_test_privacy_failure.unit: processed covert-test request improperly released without redacting personally identifiable information

processing_delay_example.value: Navy average FOIA processing time increased from 1.6 to 55.5 days during the review period; officials attributed challenges partly to staffing limitations

system_complexity.value: Defense Health Agency processors must identify health records across multiple data systems and review them for personally identifiable information, with system issues and complex workflows challenging requests

corrective_action.unit: open GAO recommendations, including workforce planning and opportunities to streamline health-record request systems

claimant_conversion.unit: requester receipt, correction, privacy harm, litigation cost, health-care continuity, disability or benefits decision, trust, or durable system improvement

observations.method: Structured extraction from GAO-27-107784, including DOD policies and processes, administrative breach data, site visits, interviews, and a covert test of 26 requests. Breach exposure, test processing, time delay, system complexity, recommendations, and claimant outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The covert test is a small, designed test and not a population estimate. The reported improper-release count is an administrative total and the public record does not link each release to a claimant outcome. Processing-time examples and system descriptions do not establish average performance across all services or records.
observations.subgroup: Service members and veterans requesting personnel, health, performance, training, or other records, including requesters whose records contain sensitive personally identifiable information.
observations.counterinterpretation: A single improper release in a small covert test does not measure the overall breach rate, and delays may reflect request complexity or lawful review requirements; conversely, policies and procedures can exist while staffing and multi-system workflows still expose requesters to delay or disclosure risk.

related_sources.claim: The official accessible report contains the breach, covert-test, processing-time, system-complexity, and recommendation findings.
The official GAO report PDF provides the full review of DOD personnel and health-record release controls.

boundary: This record advances a bounded service-member record request-to-privacy-and-delay route. It does not establish population breach prevalence, requester-level receipt, correction, privacy harm, litigation cost, health-care continuity, benefits decisions, trust, or completed corrective action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical GAO product URL string used as a stable source identifier; accessible report and PDF links are retained for reproduction.
